title: Well-definedness of the sectionwise exchange rule
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with arrows $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, and let $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$. Use inverse and direct images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Write $P_g(f_*F)$ for the presheaf inverse image whose sheafification is $g^{-1}f_*F$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For an etale $V\to Y'$, a presheaf representative is a triple $(W,a,s)$ with $W\to Y$ etale, $a:V\to Y'\times_YW$ over $Y'$, and $s\in F(X\times_YW)$. Its class in $(g^{-1}f_*F)(V)$ means the image of this presheaf representative under sheafification; no global representability of every sheaf section is asserted.

Put $K=X\times_YW$ and $A=X'\times_{Y'}V$. The square and $a$ induce $\ell_a:A\to X'\times_XK$ over $X'$. The sectionwise rule sends $(W,a,s)$ to
$$
 \ell_a^*\bigl(\eta_{g',F}(K)(s)\bigr)\in (g'^{-1}F)(A)=(f'_*g'^{-1}F)(V),
$$
where $\eta_{g',F}:F\to g'_*g'^{-1}F$ is the inverse-image adjunction unit. This is the precise meaning of restriction followed by sheafification along $A\to K$. This rule extends to a morphism $g^{-1}f_*F\to f'_*g'^{-1}F$, so its value depends only on the sheafified class, and that morphism is the underived exchange $\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. Equivalently, its adjunct under $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ is $g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f\circ\theta_\square$.

proof.text: Work on the small skeletons of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme map $u$, let $b_u$ be the etale base-change functor. It preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], so [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-sets-left-exact] gives the presheaf inverse image $P_uH$ by the filtered colimit of $H(W)$ over pairs $(W,a:V\to b_uW)$; restriction in $V$ precomposes $a$. Its presheaf-adjunction unit is the coprojection at $(W,\mathrm{id}_{b_uW})$. After sheafification this is the sheaf-adjunction unit: indeed the composite of the presheaf adjunction and the sheafification adjunction has hom bijection $\operatorname{Hom}((P_uH)^\#,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(P_uH,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(H,u_*Q)$, whose unit is precisely that coprojection followed by sheafification. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] to identify this construction and its adjunction with abelian inverse image. Thus the underlying presheaf of $P_g(f_*F)$ has representatives $(W,a,s)$ as stated, and the image of $(W,\mathrm{id},s)$ is $\eta_{g,f_*F}(W)(s)$.

proof.text:
Write $Q=g'^{-1}F$ and $B=f'_*Q$. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $B(V)=Q(A)$. Given $(W,a,s)$, put $r_{W,a}(s)=\ell_a^*(\eta_{g',F}(K)(s))$. This is a group homomorphism in $s$. To check a transition, take $h:W_1\to W_2$ with $a_2=(\mathrm{id}_{Y'}\times h)a_1$ and put $k=\mathrm{id}_X\times h:K_1\to K_2$. Naturality of the unit gives
$$ (\mathrm{id}_{X'}\times_Xk)^*\eta_{g',F}(K_2)(s)=\eta_{g',F}(K_1)(k^*s). $$
Since $\ell_{a_2}=(\mathrm{id}_{X'}\times_Xk)\ell_{a_1}$, restriction once more yields $r_{W_2,a_2}(s)=r_{W_1,a_1}(k^*s)$. These are exactly the colimit relations. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the maps induce $r_V:P_g(f_*F)(V)\to B(V)$. For $v:V_1\to V_2$, the map $A_1\to A_2$ satisfies $\ell_{a v}=\ell_a\circ(\mathrm{id}_{X'}\times v)$, so $r$ commutes with restriction. Thus $r$ is a presheaf morphism of abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 00VE, lemma-adjoints-u, proof: cocone given by restriction maps; applied to etale base change

proof.text:
The target $B=f'_*Q$ is a sheaf by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Apply [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] in abelian groups to $r$ to obtain a unique $\psi:g^{-1}f_*F\to B$ with $\psi\circ j=r$, where $j:P_g(f_*F)\to g^{-1}f_*F$ is the sheafification map. In particular equal sheafified classes have equal images under the sectionwise rule, even when equality is not visible in the presheaf colimit. Evaluate at $V=b_gW$, $a=\mathrm{id}$. The map $\ell_a$ is then the canonical identification of the iterated fibre products. Step 1 shows that $\psi\eta_{g,f_*F}$ is the morphism
$$ \delta:f_*F\xrightarrow{f_*\eta_{g',F}}f_*g'_*Q\xrightarrow{d}g_*f'_*Q, $$
where $d$ is induced by $(X'\times_X(X\times_YW))\cong X'\times_{Y'}(Y'\times_YW)$. This identifies the adjunct of $\psi$ under $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ without assuming global representatives for arbitrary sheaf sections.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint; Tag 00VE, unit coprojection and adjunct formula

proof.text:
We now compare with the fixed categorical exchange. Put $H=f_*F$. Under the composite adjunction $f'^{-1}g^{-1}\dashv g_*f'_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the adjunct of $f'^{-1}\psi$ followed by the counit $\varepsilon_{f',Q}$ is $g_*\psi\circ\eta_{g,H}=\delta$. Indeed taking the first adjunct under $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ gives $\psi$ by its triangle identity, and taking the second gives this displayed formula. The square isomorphism is the one obtained by identifying both composite inverse images with $(fg')^{-1}=(gf')^{-1}$, as in [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The unit equation (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] therefore says that, under these same composite adjunctions, the adjunct of
$$ r_0=g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F}\circ\theta_{\square,H} $$
is
$$ d\circ f_*g'_*(g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ f_*(\eta_{g',f^{-1}H})\circ\eta_{f,H}. $$
Here $d:f_*g'_*Q\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*f'_*Q$ is exactly the fibre-product identification of step 3: part (1) of the composition node gives its components. This use of the specified unit-compatible composition isomorphisms fixes the orientation of the mate.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites; unit-compatible composition and the explicit composite adjunction

proof.text:
Naturality of $\eta_{g'}$ at $\varepsilon_{f,F}:f^{-1}H\to F$ gives
$$ g'_*(g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ\eta_{g',f^{-1}H}=\eta_{g',F}\circ\varepsilon_{f,F}. $$
Consequently the last expression in step 4 equals
$$ d\circ f_*\eta_{g',F}\circ f_*\varepsilon_{f,F}\circ\eta_{f,H}=d\circ f_*\eta_{g',F}=\delta, $$
using the triangle identity $f_*\varepsilon_{f,F}\circ\eta_{f,f_*F}=\mathrm{id}_{f_*F}$. The composite-adjunction hom bijection is injective, so $\varepsilon_{f',Q}\circ f'^{-1}\psi=r_0$. By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], $\Ex^0_{\square,F}$ is the unique morphism with exactly this adjunct. Therefore $\psi=\Ex^0_{\square,F}$, proving both the stated section formula and its independence of the representative.

Step 3 handles equality after sheafification correctly through the universal property.
